entityName: Budapest University of Technology and Economics - Department of Aeronautics and Naval Architecture
entityDescription:
The Department of Aeronautics and Naval Architecture was established more than 70 years ago as Department of Aircraft. Today it has 19 full time teaching-researcher staff of which 12 has PhD degrees. The Department delivers lecture on BSC, MSc and PhD levels including the fundamental sciences (fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, numerical methods, numerical optimisation, etc.) and the professional subjects on specialisation in aeronautics, air transportation,
ATM, pilot training, naval architecture and railway vehicles. There research and teaching infrastructure includes several laboratories (fluid and thermal machines, UAS lab and workshop, CFD lab and training centre, advanced instrumentation lab) and is also equipped with full size flight simulators for scientific purposes (with B737 and A320 controls in left and right seats), Mechatronix Ascent FNTP II flight simulator applied in the pilot training program, small computer controlled gas turbine, small water channel, load and test bench, track qualification vehicles, thermal cameras, motion capture system, and several others.
The Department has been involved in more than 25 EU supported projects including the SESAR and CleanSky megaprojects, the EPATS, SAT-Rdmp, Sinbad, Pplane, Esposa, Neli, Innovate, SmartPolis, several national projects, including SafeFly – developing small 4 seater aircraft, and Idea-e, working on the conceptual design of small 4-seater electric aircraft and large cargo hybrid UAV. The Department was also involved in developing design for various yachts (such as the special demonstration yacht Penelope), and aircraft including the leading advisory role in the development of the Corvus Racer for the Red Bull AirRace.
The leading staff members served as project coordinators and project managers for the L1 level Gabriel project which developed the maglev supported take-off and landing of undercarriage-less aircraft. This project was managed to finish in the planned time frame without any changes in the
defined description of work. The Department members have significant experience in international conference organisation, and work with high level international bodies, such as the International Forum for Aviation Research (IFAR). The department has a long term and successful working relationship many European universities, institutions and companies, including DLR, ONERA, CIRA, NLR, TU München, Aachen, Delft, HungaroControl, Knorr-Bremse, Siemens, and several
others. The department has strong skills in concept exploration, operational concept development, developing disruptive technologies and solutions and the combination of engineering solutions with economic and innovation aspects. Staff members are publishing 35 – 40 articles yearly.

entityName: TUM - CHAIR OF SCIENTIFIC COMPUTING IN COMPUTER SCIENCE (SCCS)
entityDescription: “The most scientifically important and economically promising research frontiers in the 21st century will be conquered by those most skilled with advanced computing technologies and computational science applications.” This central statement from the 2005 President’s IT Advisory Committee report from the US also outlines the chair’s focus fields in research and teaching: the algorithmics of scientific and high-performance computing as well as applications of numerical simulation. The spectrum extends from efficient numerical algorithms (discretization of partial differential equations, fast linear solvers, high-dimensional numerics, sparse grids, image processing, adaptivity, and hardware-awareness) via parallel and distributed computing (parallel algorithms, parallelization, load balancing, and Grid computing) as well as the embedding of simulation tasks up to simulation scenarios from various fields (fluid dynamics, fluid-structure interaction, chemical engineering, traffic, finance, or quantum chemistry). Our research projects, due to the tasks’ complexity, are typically tackled in multi-disciplinary cooperation and, thus, cover almost the entire simulation pipeline.

Bauhaus Luftfahrt e.V. has been founded in 2005 as an independent non-profit research institution for long term research in aviation by the three aerospace companies EADS (today Airbus Group), Liebherr-Aerospace and MTU Aero Engines as well as the Bavarian Ministry for Economic Affairs. In January 2012, IABG-Industrieanlagen-Betriebsgesellschaft became the latest member of the institution.
The non-profit institution is an internationally-oriented think tank. The team of around 35 scientists deals with the future of mobility in general and with the future of air travel in particular. The goal of the research work is to consider the complex system of aviation from different points of view. Reserach projects are aimed to consider technical, economic, social and ecological aspects holistically. Researchers from a variety of domains and expertise areas are jointly working on novel technologies, concepts and processes which could change the way aviation is operated in the coming decades.
The current strategy has put the focus on strengthening the five leading themes:
 „Visionary Aircraft Concepts“,
 „Ecological Perspectives of Aviation, Sustainability and Alternative Energies“,
 „Future Technologies and Innovation PotentialsInnovation Potentials“,
 „Socio-economic and Political Drivers of Future Aviation“, and
 „Knowledge Management“.
Along those leading themes, Bauhaus Luftfahrt achieved worldwide recognition and to became a nucleus for international research networks with the main focus on the first three themes.
The following key objectives were pursued in the research work at Bauhaus Luftfahrt in the past years:
- Development of concepts for innovative solutions and their implementation roadmaps,
- Publication of results in the form of conference contributions and journal articles as well as
- Organization of scientific conferences, seminars and workshops
- Generation of intellectual properties and patents.

The IDF is a public/private partnership led by the insurance industry and supported by international organisations. The IDF was conceived and proposed at a meeting of the Political Champions Group for Disaster Resilience (PCG) on the margins of the UN General Assembly in 2013. A Task Force was formed and produced a detailed Concept Note that outlined its need, purpose and potential operation. O.C.E. Technology is a European company setup to develop products and services for high-reliability embedded systems. Its founders bring together many years’ engineering, academic and business experience developing successful hardware and software products. The company is supported by the Irish government and has strong cooperation with the European Space agency in the development of unique innovative products to improve productivity of embedded software developers.
The management team has an established track record in the successful development and sales of processor ICs and boards to large OEMs (Siemens, Intel) and the associated software and operating systems.
Located in south Dublin OCE’s products include software productivity tools for SPARC and ARM embedded processors, high-reliability system-on-chip (SOC) devices, system-in-package (SIP) memories, and satellite subsystems.
OCE, in cooperation with the European Space Agency (ESA), developed a SOC debug software tool and high-reliability category B operating system for the Space market. The requirements of this market are similar to those of other embedded system markets such as automotive and medical. The company has setup a global distribution network and is pursuing an aggressive expansion programme.
OCE’s quad-core rad-hard SPARC chip is the highest performance of its type commercially available and is already successfully flying on 15 satellites. In 2021 OCE launched a high performance rad-tolerant AI chip with quadcore ARM, and octa core GPU and neural network accelerator cores. OCE’s SIP process is one of only two similar processes in the world. OCE offers a custom SIP design service for companies wishing to produce proprietary OBCs or systems housed in a SIP package. OCE also offers a range of satellite subsystems with many years heritage.
